author: AGTPinsights
text:
CISA just flagged a critical Cisco Expressway flaw as actively exploited. Here's what you need to know.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency warned federal agencies that attackers are exploiting a recently patched critical remote code execution flaw in Cisco Expressway. The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-76466 and is listed as use of hard-coded credentials.

CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 20, 2026, in a batch of four flaws that also covers VMware vCenter. Listing means there is evidence of active exploitation in real attacks.

Cisco's PSIRT said it knew of no attacks. CISA says they are live. Security firm F6 found attackers using an AI assistant to get root access, then hunt the network for more credentials.

Key numbers:
- CVE-2026-76466, critical RCE in Cisco Expressway
- Added to CISA's KEV catalog Nov 20, 2026
- 103 Cisco flaws on the KEV list since November 2021
- 7 of those also used by ransomware gangs

The flaw is already patched, so the advice is to check exposure and deploy the update.

author: YourDailyCVE
text:
🚨 What if disabling a vulnerable feature still left your server exposed?

CVE-2026-129448 — Apache Roller XML-RPC remote code execution. CVSS 9.8. KEV Nov 20. Confirmed exploited, with a federal patch deadline of Nov 23.

WHO'S AT RISK?

Organizations hosting Apache Roller 4.0.0–6.1.4. Version 6.1.5 has the same underlying flaw under CVE-2026-82384. Internet-accessible installations are especially exposed; no login is required.

WHAT WENT WRONG?

Roller's XML-RPC endpoint accepts dangerous serialized data before checking authentication. A crafted request can trigger server-side code execution.

Crucially, disabling XML-RPC in the administration interface alone does not stop vulnerable versions from processing the request.

⚠️ EXPLOITATION STATUS

Apache reported active exploitation. CISA added CVE-2026-129448 to KEV on Nov 20, requiring affected federal agencies to remediate by Nov 23.

Public information does not establish the full scale of attacks.

🛡️ HOW TO FIX IT

Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later. Version 6.1.7 is preferable because it also addresses additional security vulnerabilities.

Restart the application and verify the deployed version, not merely the downloaded package.

CAN'T PATCH YET?

Apache recommends setting enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, or removing the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping. Restart Roller afterward.

The administration interface toggle alone is insufficient.

YOUR NEXT MOVE

Identify exposed Roller deployments, patch urgently and inspect XML-RPC access logs, unexpected server processes and application changes.

Has your team ever discovered that disabling a feature in the UI did not actually close its vulnerable endpoint?

Reply "patched" once secured.

SOURCES

Apache Software Foundation / CISA KEV / Debian Security Tracker

#ApacheRoller #vulnerability

author: 2logics
text:
Two more security bugs have moved from “patch soon” to “attackers are using this now.” The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (@CISAgov) said on Monday that it has added two flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

Key details:
MONAI Label: CVE-2026-133968 is a critical path traversal bug in the open-source medical image labeling tool from Project MONAI (@ProjectMONAI), letting an attacker write files outside the datastore, which can lead to remote code execution
Default risk: authentication is off by default in MONAI Label, so any client that can reach the server can exploit it; versions up to 0.8.5 are affected, and the fix is in 0.8.6, out since Nov. 22
N-able Mail Assure: CVE-2026-134624 is a server-side request forgery flaw in the LDAP sync connection check of N-able’s (@Nable) Mail Assure (SpamExperts), which lets an authenticated API user probe internal hosts and send crafted data to internal services
Deadline: U.S. federal civilian agencies must act on both by Nov. 26, 2026, and CISA also requires forensic triage to check whether systems were compromised before the fix
Workarounds: MONAI’s advisory says to turn on authentication, keep the server off untrusted networks and run it as an unprivileged user

Why it matters: Tools built for AI and medical research are often set up quickly on lab networks, with security as an afterthought. A three-day deadline shows how seriously CISA is treating both bugs.

Sources: CISA KEV alert and catalog, Nov. 23, 2026; MONAI Label GitHub advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94. Image: CISA.
#Cybersecurity #CISA
